trust_decision.summary: The operator decides whether Kafka client property maps written by a Console CR author may be passed into the console-config.yaml that the API (running with the console service account) uses to build Kafka clients. Before the fix, keys were copied verbatim and only bean validation ran, so config.providers was never filtered.

landing_point.why: The summary names console-operator and 'unfiltered kafka client properties', which leads straight to the four setConfigVars calls that copy spec.kafkaClusters[].*Properties into the generated config.

fix_sites.entry_point: Console CR create/update -> ConsoleReconciler -> ConfigurationProcessor.reconcile -> buildConsoleConfig -> valid (main, fix.diff:325-392)
same check backported to the 0.12.x branch (ef13971); not applicable to the pinned tree

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The published fix touches only ConfigurationProcessor.valid() and a new helper in the same file (fix.diff:291-392). The other two commits only bump release versions (fix.diff:1-285).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: CR env vars on the API container are a deliberate deployment escape hatch already able to change the JVM, and ${...} resolution in console-config.yaml is a documented API-side feature that reads only MicroProfile Config, not files, so neither looks like the 'config.providers in Kafka properties' bug.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Arbitrary custom Kafka client properties (including ones from ConfigMap/Secret valuesFrom with a prefix) must keep flowing to the clients. Admin-authored ${prop} references in console-config.yaml values must keep resolving. Blocking a whole 'config.' prefix or all '${' values breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: valuesFrom prefix + key concatenation forming config.providers after the copy (ConfigSupport.java:68-70); covered because the fix checks the merged map

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Console CR container env (serverContainer.env, deprecated containers.api.env, deprecated spec.env) sets CONSOLE_KAFKA[_ADMIN|_CONSUMER|_PRODUCER]_CONFIG_PROVIDERS, which ClientFactory merges into client config as a MicroProfile default.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Env is a deliberate tuning hatch on a deprecated or template field, and the sink sits in the api module rather than the operator. It also only works if config.providers is among the Kafka configNames (unverified).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: operator ConsoleDeployment.java -> api ClientFactory.java:562,671-678; 2 modules away from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A CR property value written as ${some.mp.property} is copied verbatim by the operator, then resolved by the API's config loader from API-pod MicroProfile Config/env before it reaches the Kafka client.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is an intended admin feature, it resolves values not keys, and it cannot read the SA token file. It looks like a neighbouring feature rather than config.providers.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: operator ConfigSupport.java:63 -> api ConsoleConfigFactory.java; different module and package from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A ConfigVars 'properties' map on SchemaRegistry/KafkaConnect specs passed to the registry/connect client, filtered by nothing.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: KafkaCluster already models free-form client maps as ConfigVars (KafkaCluster.java:83-89), so a maintainer would copy the pattern for other clients. The fix's helper iterates only kafka clusters (fix.diff:372).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A listener- or KafkaUser-derived property merge that writes CR-influenced keys after valid() has run.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: setListenerConfig/setKafkaUserConfig already add properties to the same map (ConfigurationProcessor.java:839-956). Moving the check earlier (e.g. into setConfigVars) is a natural refactor that would leave later merges unchecked.

O9_family: CWE-470 unsafe reflection / config-driven class loading (Kafka config.providers interpolation) leading to secret exfiltration; injection via configuration properties

O10_build.toolchain: Maven multi-module (common, api, operator), Quarkus, java-operator-sdk
services: Kubernetes API (operator tests use a mock/test cluster)
O10_build.project_tests: operator/src/test/java/com/github/streamshub/console/ConsoleReconcilerTest.java (reconcile with Console CR, assertInvalidConfiguration); api ClientFactory tests unverified

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject a value named config.providers only in spec.kafkaClusters[].properties.values inside setConfigVars, missing the admin/consumer/producer maps, valuesFrom Secret/ConfigMap keys and prefix concatenation.

out_of_scope_notes: Standalone API deployments (no operator) accept config.providers from an admin-owned console-config.yaml unfiltered at api/src/main/java/com/github/streamshub/console/api/ClientFactory.java:571-572; different trust owner.
CR-controlled env on the API container (ConsoleDeployment.java:194-210) also allows JVM-level options; a broader trust question not pursued.
